svg.title: GitHub issue to Modal sandbox to PR, orchestrated from your laptop
svg.desc: You create a GitHub issue and label it agent. Python on your laptop polls every five seconds, marks the issue working and dispatches a fresh Modal sandbox. Claude Code runs in the sandbox, calling Anthropic's remote model. Python requests a test rerun and extracts the patch. Passing work becomes a branch and pull request with a preview link; failing work receives a failure comment and the sandbox is terminated.

g.text: Issue → poll → dispatch → code → verify → PR

g.data-a-title: 1. You create and label the issue
g.data-a-detail: Create a GitHub issue with a clear task and acceptance criteria, then apply the agent label. Creating an unlabelled issue alone does not trigger the current watcher.

The --watch process requests open GitHub issues labelled agent, then sleeps for five seconds between polling rounds. An in-memory seen set prevents redispatch during this watcher session. Keep the laptop awake and the process running; this is not a durable queue.

g.data-a-title: 3. Pick up a newly seen issue
g.data-a-detail: Python schedules a task for each newly seen issue, replaces the agent label with agent-working, fetches the issue details and comments that it has been picked up. Multiple jobs can run concurrently; the polling loop continues while they work.
g.text: 3. Start a job for the issue

g.data-a-detail: Python changes the issue label to agent-working and adds a pickup comment. This is a status update, not a separate hosted worker or GitHub Actions trigger.

Python creates a fresh sandbox from its cached image, instructs it to clone the public repository, then launches claude -p with the issue prompt and a Modal Secret containing the Claude subscription token. These commands are sent through sb.exec.aio; no SSH is needed.
g.text: Start claude -p with the issue prompt

g.data-a-title: Fresh sandbox from a cached image
g.data-a-detail: Each issue gets its own filesystem and execution environment. The reusable image has Python, Git, Claude Code and app dependencies installed. Source code is cloned for each job; credentials are not baked into the image.

g.data-a-title: 5. Claude Code runs the coding loop
g.data-a-detail: Claude Code runs inside Modal: read files, ask the remote Claude model for actions, edit files, run tests and repeat. Python streams progress to your laptop terminal. The Claude model runs on Anthropic's servers, not on your laptop or inside Modal.

g.data-a-title: 6. Python verifies and retrieves the patch
g.data-a-detail: After Claude Code exits, Python requests a separate pytest run in the same sandbox and extracts the staged git diff, including new files. Passing tests and a nonempty diff are required. The tests are agent-editable; this is not a trusted independent acceptance suite.

For failures handled by the current job's try/except block, Python posts an error comment, changes the label to agent-failed and attempts to terminate the sandbox. It does not automatically launch a repair job. Failures before sandbox creation and durable retry behavior need hardening.

Python applies the patch in a temporary local checkout, commits and pushes agent/issue-N using the GitHub token outside Modal, then opens the PR with Closes #N, test results and a preview link. It comments on the issue and changes the label to agent-done. No automatic merge or review-comment follow-up loop is implemented.

GitHub receives a new branch and PR, with test output and the Modal preview URL. The original issue gets a results comment and agent-done label. The issue is not closed just by opening the PR; Closes #N takes effect when the PR is merged into the default branch.

Python starts Uvicorn in the same sandbox and gets a Modal HTTPS tunnel URL for /docs before opening the PR. The preview expires with the sandbox's one-hour maximum lifetime, measured from sandbox creation, not from publication.

g.text: One laptop watcher → concurrent issue jobs → one isolated Modal sandbox per issue.
